I am a biophysicist trained in physics and statistical physics. I defended my PhD
in 2025 at ESPCI Paris (Gulliver) and Sorbonne Université (LJP), supervised by
Clément Nizak and Olivier Rivoire. My thesis, *Statistical design of specificity
in S1A serine proteases*, combined high-throughput microfluidic screening of
trypsin mutants with statistical modelling: analysis of deep-sequencing data
(Illumina, Nanopore), kinetic and Bayesian models of sorting experiments, and
experimental tests of Potts-model predictions.

I am interested in simple yet powerful models applied to complex biological
data: statistical physics of sequences and evolution, quantitative ecology,
Bayesian inference and interpretable machine learning.

## Education

- PhD in Physics, ESPCI Paris / Sorbonne Université (2025)
- MSc Biological Systems: Physical Concepts, Université Paris-Saclay (2022)
- Engineering degrees, ESPCI Paris and Institut d'Optique (2022)

Each post is a self-contained project on public data, with its code on GitHub.
